Hi Diana / Marissa —

Thanks for the context — below are recommended architecture and concrete sizing heuristics you can use to validate against the worksheet. Happy to walk through each item on the call.

1) Integration & SDK/auth patterns- SDK: use the Redwood client with client-side request batching for search frontends where feasible (group small parallel requests into a single multi-call); enable client retry with exponential backoff and jitter.
- Auth: mTLS between your service and Redwood ingress for dedicated control plane + short-lived bearer tokens for app-level calls. We'll also support IP allow lists and support issuing client certs if you want fully managed mTLS.
- Routing: recommend regional routing (us-west primary) with automatic fallback to a smaller-capacity variant in us-east if primary pool is saturated; configure model-variant policy for quality-first on user-facing reranker.

2) Structured output / tool-calling patterns- For structured outputs (tool-calling/function-calling), return machine-readable JSON from the model and validate schemas at the application layer; use function-calling to constrain output when driving downstream product flows.

3) Embeddings + reranker pattern- Architecture: separate embeddings service (batch for indexing) + online embedding generation for live queries if needed. Use ANN index for candidate retrieval then a dedicated reranker endpoint (smaller batch sizes, tight latency).
- Recommendation: run embeddings on a mixed pool (FP16 quantized) and reranker on a CPU/GPU mix depending on model size. Consider an L2-normalization cache for frequent queries.

4) Dedicated capacity autoscaling & sizing heuristics- Throughput assumptions: average tokens/request (in reranker path) ~600 tokens total (prompt + context + completion).
- Concurrency per GPU: for modern transformer LLMs and our optimized runtime we target 6–10 concurrent in-flight requests per GPU for latency-sensitive reranker calls. For safety use 8 concurrency/GPU as baseline.
- Token throughput per GPU: estimate ~1200 tokens/sec per GPU for the selected model family under 8-concurrency baseline (runbook will include measured benchmarks).
- Pool sizing: steady-state QPS 200 -> requests/sec * tokens/request = 200 * 600 = 120k tokens/sec. With 1200 tokens/sec per GPU -> ~100 GPUs (!) — this is a conservative number because reranker calls are smaller in practice; you will want to optimize by lowering tokens/request, using smaller reranker models, and increasing batching for non-latency-critical paths.
- Practical approach: separate pools: small, low-latency pool (8–16 GPUs) sized to handle ~30–50% of peak with p95 SLO; a larger, autoscaling bulk pool for background / precompute work.

5) Queueing & burst handling- Use a prioritized token-based queue: each request is scored by estimated token cost and priority (user-facing high priority). The queue should admit requests into the GPU pool respecting SLOs and letting lower-priority work wait.
- Warm pool: keep a small warm pool of GPU instances (minutes warm) to handle bursts; use spot instances for bulk pool with fallback.
- Autoscaling policy: combine schedule-based scaling (for known sale events) and reactive scaling with headroom target (e.g., keep 20% free capacity to avoid cold starts).

6) Concrete next steps & deliverables I can prepare before the call- A recommended pool sizing spreadsheet filled from your real token-per-request numbers (I can update the attached XLS).
- A suggested autoscaling policy + example Terraform snippets for pool sizing and warm pool.
- Network egress and mTLS config doc with sample cert rotation cadence.

Questions for you ahead of the call:
- Can you confirm a more precise tokens-per-request for the reranker path (we used 600 above as a starting point)?
- Do you prefer a single combined pool or separated low-latency vs bulk pools?
- Who is the infra owner for firewall/evidence so we can share IPs and any CSP requirements?

I attached an updated sizing worksheet (redwood-dedicated-queue-sizing.xlsx) with the above baseline assumptions. Suggested time: Mon, 30 Aug 2026 10:00 AM PT for a 45-minute deep dive — does that work?
